description: J On The Beach is a developer conference held in Torremolinos on the Costa del Sol, bringing together engineers working with big data, distributed systems and the JVM ecosystem. The 2026 edition runs across two days in late October, combining technical deep dives with workshops led by practitioners rather than vendors. The conference has built a reputation for substantive content over sponsor-driven programming, attracting backend engineers, data architects and platform teams from across Europe. Sessions typically cover Kafka, Spark, Kubernetes, functional programming and the operational realities of running data infrastructure at scale. The beachside setting in southern Spain is deliberate: the organisers position it as a conference where the hallway track matters as much as the stage, with attendees staying in the same area and continuing conversations well past the closing session. For teams travelling to Torremolinos, accommodation sits within walking distance of the venue, and most international attendees arrive via Málaga airport, roughly twenty minutes away. Uphill Conf is a two-day frontend and web development conference held in Bern, Switzerland. The 2027 edition takes place at the end of April and follows the format the organisers have refined over several years: a single track, a deliberately capped audience, and speakers chosen for depth rather than name recognition. Content focuses on modern web platform work, covering frameworks, performance, accessibility and the architectural decisions behind large frontend codebases. The single-track structure means every attendee sees the same talks, which the organisers argue produces better hallway conversations than a fragmented multi-track schedule. Bern offers a compact, walkable setting with reliable rail connections from Zurich and Geneva airports, making it accessible for attendees travelling from across Europe. The conference draws a mix of Swiss engineering teams and international developers, and the smaller scale keeps it closer to a community gathering than a trade event. Agile Testing Days is one of Europe's longest-running conferences dedicated to software testing and quality engineering, held annually in Potsdam near Berlin. The 2026 edition runs across four days in November, combining tutorials, conference sessions and workshops. The programme covers test automation, exploratory testing, quality strategy, and the evolving role of testers within agile and DevOps teams. What distinguishes the event is its emphasis on practitioner experience over theory, with many sessions delivered by testers presenting work from their own organisations rather than consultants selling methodology. The conference attracts QA engineers, test architects, engineering managers and developers from across Europe, and typically runs at several hundred attendees. Potsdam sits directly outside Berlin with frequent rail connections, and most international attendees fly into Berlin Brandenburg airport. The multi-day format means nearly all attendees require accommodation for the full week. Event teams organising conferences of this length can use Hoperfy to handle hotel booking, room blocks and speaker accommodation without adding workload internally.

DITA Europe is a specialist conference focused on structured content, technical documentation and the DITA standard, held in Helsinki in February 2027. The event brings together technical writers, content strategists, documentation managers and the tooling vendors that serve them. Sessions cover content reuse, localisation workflows, single-sourcing strategy, and the practical challenges of migrating legacy documentation into structured formats. The audience skews towards enterprise documentation teams in software, manufacturing and medical device industries, where regulatory requirements make structured content management a necessity rather than a preference. DITA Europe is deliberately small compared to general content conferences, which keeps the technical level high and makes it useful for teams facing specific implementation problems. Helsinki is well connected to the rest of Europe through Helsinki-Vantaa airport, and the February timing means most attendees book accommodation close to the venue rather than commuting. Conference organisers managing specialist events with international attendees can work with Hoperfy to arrange hotel booking and speaker housing.

Euroanaesthesia is the annual congress of the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care, taking place in Copenhagen from 29 to 31 May 2027. It is the largest anaesthesiology meeting in Europe, drawing several thousand clinicians, researchers and trainees from across the continent and beyond. The scientific programme covers perioperative medicine, intensive care, pain management, patient safety and emerging research across the specialty, delivered through plenary lectures, abstract presentations, workshops and hands-on skills sessions. The congress also functions as the primary European meeting point for medical device and pharmaceutical companies serving the field, with a substantial exhibition running alongside the scientific sessions. Copenhagen offers strong international air connections and a compact city centre, though a congress of this scale places significant pressure on hotel availability, and attendees typically book several months in advance.
